For those wondering the powder is formed into tiny cylinders because that has the optimal mix of burning quickly and evenly.

Huh Wrong. Powder come in three shapes. Cylinders (often with a hole in the middle) spheres, and Flakes. The speed of burning and amount of gas produced is determined by surface area.

In a solid cylinder the surface area decreases as the powder burns. The cylinder shape allows for an initial burst of gas that tapers off as the cylinder diameter is reduced. When a hole is placed in the center of the cylinder the surface area burning rate remains constant. The decrease of outside surface area is made up for by the increase of surface area of the inside hole. The biggest draw back of cylindrical powder is there are constancy of loading problems with automated loading equipment.

The next shape is the spherical powder. It has the initial burst of gas like the cylindrical powder which tapers off as the sphere gets smaller. However the spherical powder is the ideal form of powder to flow through automated loading equipment. The 7.62 X 51 uses spherical powder for consistency shot after shot. Also spherical powder has a longer storage life than cylindrical powders.

Flake powder give a more consistent burning pattern as the surface area does not decrease markedly until consumed. Flake powders are not kind to Automatic loading equipment. Flaked powder also has another advantage is that it does not move around much in the case so recoil of the weapon won't pack the powder against the primer hole when the round is in the magazine and the weapon is fired.
